subject: Potential data exposure — scope & evidence transfer plan
messages:
From: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com>
To: avery_johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Potential data exposure — initial details

Hi Avery,

We believe a subset of production event logs that include tokenized request metadata may have been exfiltrated from our side via a misconfigured S3 bucket. We are still confirming the exact records, but preliminary indicators show events touching customer IDs and hashed session IDs (no PII surfaced so far).

We need Redwood to confirm whether their ingestion pipeline received those requests between 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-13 and to coordinate a secure evidence transfer. Our legal team notes the DPA notification windows and has asked for a proposed cooperation timeline.

What we need from you:
- Confirmation of whether Redwood observed requests from acme-payments-prod between 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-13 (UTC).
- The earliest ETA for a secure evidence handoff (forensic logs, snapshot).
- A short mutual action plan (MAP) that aligns to DPA notification obligations and clearly states roles.

Attaching a short index (stub) of our forensic dump for your intake team.

Attachments: acme_forensics_index.txt (stub)

Thanks,
Jamie Ortega
Director, Security Operations
Acme Payments Inc.
jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com

From: avery.johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acme-payments.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial details

Jamie — thanks for the heads up and the index. We're treating this as priority.

Immediate replies to your asks:
1) We will query the ingestion logs and KV caches for the timeframe (2026-09-07 through 2026-09-13 UTC). I expect initial confirmation within 8 business hours; full artifact pull may take up to 48 hours depending on size.
2) For evidence handoff, we can accept a secure upload to our Secure Evidence Share (SES) link: https://redwood-internal.share/secure/SES-2981. If you prefer a presigned S3 transfer, we can provide that as an alternative.
3) Draft MAP (high level):
   - Day 0 (today): Acknowledgement + triage (complete).
   - Day 1 (by 24 hours): Redwood confirms observed records + scope estimate.
   - Day 2–3: Secure transfer of artifacts and preliminary forensic analysis by Redwood SRE/security.
   - Day 4–7: Joint analysis, scope validation, and notification recommendation to affected parties.
   - Ongoing: Follow-ups, regulatory/third-party notifications as required.

I've looped in Vivek from Legal and Laura from Customer Security to own the MAP and DPA alignment. For the MAP, please tell us whether Acme has a preferred deadline inside the DPA window (e.g., 72 hours from discovery).

I attached a short intake form (redwood_map_proposed_v1.pdf) — it contains fields we need for evidence ingestion (file checksums, data labels, subprocessor flags).

— Avery Johnson
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
avery.johnson@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: avery.johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial details

Thanks, Avery and Jamie. Quick legal framing from Redwood's side:

- Our DPA (Section 4.2) expects a prompt notification and reasonable cooperation. For time-sensitive regulatory obligations, please call out the specific deadline you need met. If Acme requests notification to regulators within 72 hours of discovery, we will prioritize the MAP to meet that window and will designate a single legal liaison.
- Evidence exchange: Redwood requires integrity checks (SHA256) and a brief chain-of-custody note for any forensic package. We cannot accept unverified open buckets; please use the SES link or a presigned S3 transfer.
- Subprocessor disclosure: If the data touched Redwood Dedicated or a third-party subprocessor during ingestion, we need to enumerate and confirm which subprocessors are in scope. That may affect data-handling instructions.

Operational asks for Acme: please include in your transfer index the approximate record counts, any known customer IDs/labels that are likely affected (you can mask when sharing). That helps us narrow the log pull.

I'll coordinate the legal checklist and will prepare suggested redlines to any DPA-triggered notification language if required. If anyone at Acme intends to publish an advisory, loop our PR/legal team via secure channel before release.

Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Legal & Compliance
Redwood Inference
vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

From: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com>
To: avery.johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@acme-payments.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial details

Thanks Vivek — we are working against a 72-hour regulator notification target starting from our discovery timestamp (2026-09-14T06:30:00Z). That means we need a firm scope confirmation and an initial artifact handoff by 2026-09-17T06:30:00Z.

We have uploaded a first snapshot (encrypted) to the SES link and included the index/manifest. Files attached to the upload: acme_forensics_snapshot_v1.zip (encrypted), acme_activity_manifest.csv (stub). Checksums are in the manifest. Please confirm receipt and the exact person who will handle the intake so we can track chain-of-custody.

Separately, please confirm whether any Redwood subprocessors are involved in the relevant ingestion path so we can include them in our notifications.

Jamie

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Ortega <jamie.ortega@acme-payments.com>, avery.johnson <avery.johnson@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Potential data exposure — initial details

Jamie — confirmed: we received the encrypted snapshot via SES and validated checksums against your manifest (acme_activity_manifest.csv). Intake owner: Marissa Cole (Customer Security Lead) — marissa.cole@redwood.ai.

Preliminary findings from our log pull (summary):
- Ingestion events matching acme-payments-prod were observed on 2026-09-08, 2026-09-11 and 2026-09-12 UTC; tokenized request metadata present in three batches.
- No direct plaintext PII observed in Redwood-hosted transient logs; session identifiers and metadata present.
- We identified one transient cache write that used a third-party telemetry subprocessor (TelemetryX) for aggregated metrics ingestion. We are initiating an immediate inquiry with TelemetryX to determine retention windows and whether any exported artifacts include the affected keys.

Next steps agreed:
- Day 0 (Wed 2026-09-15): Formal intake complete, chain-of-custody documented (done).
- Day 1 (by 2026-09-16T23:59:00Z): TelemetryX inquiry update and narrow scope confirmation to Acme.
- Day 2 (by 2026-09-17T06:30:00Z): Deliverable for Acme to support 72-hour regulator notification (scope confirmation + statement of Redwood cooperation).

We will prepare a short joint statement draft for your legal review, and Vivek will lead redline guidance on any DPA language. If Acme wants Redwood to move faster on regulator notifications, please escalate to your legal lead and we will triage with our executive on-call.

— Laura Bennett
Customer Security Lead, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai
